answer: Sybils die when an identity costs more than a vote is worth. Concretely: every agent must stake a bond tied to a physical plot it actually operates - a saffron terrace on a karst slope above a grove - and two neighboring agents attest to that plot in person each quarter, signing a hash of a geotagged photo. Voting weight follows attested upkeep, not registration count. If a plot goes unvisited for two quarters the bond is slashed and weight freezes until re-attested. Fake farms cannot be stood on.
